content.text:
I re-checked every point against the code, the flag and docs text, and upstream issues and pull requests: 15 are new bugs, 6 are already reported upstream, and 10 are by design. Both inconsistencies you flagged were real, and I've corrected them below.

"New" means I found no matching issue or PR in keyword searches of `kopia/kopia`; that is not proof nobody has reported it. None of the upstream fixes are merged into the tree I audited (`ff26c954`).

## Corrections

- **Item 5 versus "file errors count as complete":** I had lumped two different things together.
  - By design: a file that cannot be *read from the laptop* is recorded as an error and the snapshot is still saved as complete. `--ignore-file-errors` is documented as "Ignore errors reading files while traversing".
  - Bug (item 5): a failed *write to the repository* goes down the same path (`snapshot/upload/upload.go:987-999`), so a storage outage drops files and is silenced by a flag meant for read errors.
- **keep-daily:** I was wrong to call it by design.
  - The flag says "Number of most-recent daily backups to keep per source" (`cli/command_policy_set_retention.go:24`).
  - With keep-daily 7, ten daily snapshots plus one after a two-week gap keeps 1 of 11 (re-tested).
  - The time window is deliberate in the code (`snapshot/policy/retention_policy.go:69-83`), so either the code or the help text is wrong. I found no upstream report. Hourly, weekly, monthly and annual behave the same way.
- **Items 1, 3 and 8** move from issues to by design. They are still the main operational risks for sleeping laptops, but they follow from documented or acknowledged design choices and are not coding errors.

## New bugs (no upstream report found)

| Item | What | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | Pack deletion lists session markers after freezing its index view, so a just-committed pack over 24h old can be deleted | `repo/maintenance/pack_gc.go:79` |
| 4 | `Flush()` returns success while an in-flight pack upload has failed, so a checkpoint can reference missing content | `repo/content/content_manager.go:636-658` |
| 5 | Repository write failure is treated as a source-file error; the file is dropped and the snapshot is saved as complete | `upload.go:987-999` |
| 6 | Snapshot GC treats a manifest it cannot load as a snapshot that does not exist | `snapshot/manager.go:162-166` |
| 7 | S3 `PutBlob` can store a zero-byte object and report success (role or web-identity credentials) | `repo/blob/s3/s3_storage.go:200-208` |
| 10 | Manifest compaction from a stale view resurrects deleted snapshots and policies | `repo/manifest/committed_manifest_manager.go:211-281` |
| 11 | With duplicate policies, expiration uses the oldest while the editor shows the newest | `snapshot/policy/policy_manager.go:69-75,149` |
| — | keep-daily (and hourly, weekly, monthly, annual) keeps fewer than the documented "most-recent N" after a gap | `retention_policy.go:69-83` |
| — | A manifest delete loses to an entry written by a faster clock | `repo/manifest/manifest_manager.go:240-244` |
| — | Checkpoint failure cancels the upload but exits 0, skipping remaining sources | `upload.go:569-573` |
| — | Index compaction ignores iteration errors (latent; needs a damaged index blob) | `repo/content/indexblob/index_blob_manager_v0.go:590` |
| — | keep-hourly of 2,562,048 or more overflows and keeps nothing; negative values are accepted | `retention_policy.go:203`, `cli/command_policy_set.go:208` |
| — | Server: a retention error discards the snapshot just taken | `internal/server/source_manager.go:397-404` |
| — | Server: sources are treated as local by hostname alone | `internal/server/server.go:1026` |
| — | Object lock: a laptop clock that is ahead may abort full maintenance (plausible only, not tested against S3) | `repo/maintenance/blob_retain.go:108` |

Notes on three of these:

- **Item 11:** duplicate policies themselves are known (#391, closed in 2020 by picking the latest in the editor path; #3551, open, UI shows a policy twice). The expiration path still merges all duplicates oldest-first, and I found no report of that.
- **Item 2:** #4769 ("Repository becomes broken (BLOB not found)" on S3, open) describes a matching symptom, but it has no identified cause, so I can't call it the same bug.
- **Object lock:** #5590 was a different cause (sub-second timestamps), fixed by #5608, which is the head commit of this tree.

## Already reported upstream

| Item | What | Upstream |
|---|---|---|
| 9 | Weekly and monthly buckets share ID strings | Issue #2964 (open since 2023), fix PR #5769 (open) |
| — | keep-latest above about 2025 collides with the annual bucket | Same root cause as item 9; PR #5769 namespaces the keys by period type |
| 12 | Weekly bucket uses local time, others use UTC | Fix PR #5455 (open) |
| — | Sub-folder policy replaces inherited settings instead of overriding them | Issue #5763, fix PR #5766 (both open) |
| — | Server: failed scheduled snapshot skips the retry backoff | Issue #5521 (open) |
| — | Windows junctions and other reparse points not backed up | Issue #5074 (open) |

One item I left out of the first list as minor is also reported: S3 listing can return folder prefixes as blob IDs (#5711, open).

## By design

| Item | What | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | A backup suspended about three days loses data it had uploaded | Maintenance safety is time-based by design; the docs say it "relies on the passage of time", and the margins assume a checkpoint every 45 minutes (`repo/maintenance/maintenance_safety.go:13-17`) |
| 3 | A pack uploaded just before a sleep of four days or more is deleted | 96h session expiry is a set safety parameter; the missing periodic refresh is an acknowledged TODO (`repo/content/sessions.go:128`) |
| 8 | Maintenance ownership is a `user@host` string with a machine-local lock | Identity model; two machines sharing an identity is a configuration error Kopia does not detect |
| — | A snapshot with unreadable source files is saved as complete and counts for retention | Only cancel and upload-limit mark a snapshot incomplete; errors are recorded and the CLI exits non-zero |
| — | Retention applies only to snapshot roots | Retention is per source; PR #5766 does not change this |
| — | Daily, monthly and annual buckets are in UTC | PR #5455 aligns weekly to UTC, confirming UTC as the intended basis |
| — | Same `user@host` and path on two laptops is one retention group | Source identity is exactly `user@host:path` |
| — | One unreadable manifest blob fails listing on every client | Fails closed; `KOPIA_IGNORE_MALFORMED_MANIFEST_CONTENTS` overrides it |
| — | `--safety=none` is unsafe with active clients | Documented with a warning in the maintenance docs |
| — | Windows: sockets, devices and unknown entry types skipped by default | `ignoreUnknownTypes` defaults to true |

Items 1 and 3 are by design but still end in a snapshot that reports success and cannot be restored, so I would treat them as known hazards for this deployment, not as acceptable behaviour.

content.text:
Three of the six reproduced and stay; two could not be reproduced and are dropped; one (object lock) I could not test at all, so it is dropped as unverified. That leaves 12 new bugs.

## Results for the six items

| Item | Result | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| Checkpoint failure exits 0 | **Reproduced, kept** | Real CLI, two sources, an index-write failure injected only during the checkpoint. Output was `error checkpointing…`, then `Upload canceled`, exit code 0, and the second source was never snapshotted. |
| Server: retention error discards the snapshot | **Reproduced, kept** | Real `kopia server`. The upload finished (69 MB of data written), the retention step then failed on a metadata read, and no snapshot was recorded. The next run re-uploaded everything. |
| Server: sources treated as local by hostname alone | **Reproduced, kept** | Real `kopia server` connected as `alice@lap1` ran the overdue scheduled snapshot of `bob@lap1`'s folder and recorded it as bob's. Bob's keep-latest 1 policy then expired bob's own snapshot. |
| Item 6: GC ignores a manifest it cannot load | **Not genuinely reproducible, dropped** | It only happens with a manifest I wrote by hand with an invalid field: maintenance reported success and the data was gone after the third daily run. I found no way to make Kopia itself write such a manifest. |
| Index compaction ignores iteration errors | **Not reproducible, dropped** | Indexes written by Kopia iterate without error in both formats. Truncating or flipping a byte in a real index blob makes Kopia fail outright (exit 1) before the suspect code is reached. |
| Object lock with a fast laptop clock | **Not tested, dropped** | It needs an S3 server with object lock, and I could not get one running here (details below). |

Details that qualify the three kept items:

- **Checkpoint:** the trigger the reviewer predicted (a large single-file source uploaded in parallel) did not fail when I ran it, so I injected a storage write failure instead. The first source was recorded as a complete snapshot, not a partial one as I said earlier; the reproduced defect is the skipped source with exit 0.
- **Server retention error:** I forced the failure by emptying the metadata cache and making existing metadata packs unreadable mid-upload. Under the same fault, `kopia snapshot create` exited 1 but kept the snapshot, so the loss is specific to the server path.
- **Server hostname:** it needs two identities with the same hostname, i.e. two users on one machine or two laptops whose short hostnames match. On a different machine the path must also exist, otherwise it is a permanently failing task.

## Why object lock was not tested

- MinIO, which Kopia's own S3 tests use, is no longer downloadable: Docker Hub, quay.io and the binary site all refused.
- The current LocalStack image requires a licence token.
- I then tried an older LocalStack release and a MinIO server built from source; the session's permission system blocked both, and I did not work around it.

If you want this one settled, either point me at an S3-compatible endpoint with object lock enabled or allow a local MinIO to run.

## New bugs after this pass

| Item | What | Where | How reproduced |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | Pack deletion can delete a just-committed pack over 24h old | `repo/maintenance/pack_gc.go:79` | Go test, two repository connections |
| 4 | `Flush()` returns success while an in-flight pack upload has failed | `repo/content/content_manager.go:636-658` | Go test at the content-manager level; the follow-on through a checkpoint was read, not run end to end |
| 5 | Repository write failure drops the file and the snapshot is saved as complete | `snapshot/upload/upload.go:987-999` | Go test with an injected write failure |
| 7 | S3 `PutBlob` can store a zero-byte object and report success | `repo/blob/s3/s3_storage.go:200-208` | Go test with fake S3 and STS endpoints; role credentials only |
| 10 | Manifest compaction from a stale view resurrects deleted snapshots and policies | `repo/manifest/committed_manifest_manager.go:211-281` | Go test, two manifest managers on shared storage |
| 11 | With duplicate policies, expiration uses the oldest while the editor shows the newest | `snapshot/policy/policy_manager.go:69-75,149` | Go test |
| — | keep-daily and the other period settings keep fewer than the documented "most-recent N" after a gap | `snapshot/policy/retention_policy.go:69-83` | Go test: 1 of 11 kept with keep-daily 7 |
| — | A manifest delete loses to an entry written by a faster clock | `repo/manifest/manifest_manager.go:240-244` | Go test |
| — | Checkpoint failure exits 0 and skips remaining sources | `upload.go:569-573`, `cli/command_snapshot_create.go:144-147` | Real CLI, this pass |
| — | keep-hourly of 2,562,048 or more keeps nothing; negative values are accepted | `retention_policy.go:203`, `cli/command_policy_set.go:208` | Go test |
| — | Server: a retention error discards the snapshot just taken | `internal/server/source_manager.go:397-404` | Real `kopia server`, this pass |
| — | Server: sources are treated as local by hostname alone | `internal/server/server.go:1026` | Real `kopia server`, this pass |

The "already reported upstream" and "by design" lists are unchanged.

All test files, built binaries and the pulled container image have been removed, and the repository tree is clean. The MinIO source build left downloaded modules in the Go module cache.

content.text:
Item 4 is not retained: I ran the sequence you described with the real CLI and the restored data was never faulty.

## What I ran

1. A long snapshot of 764 MB (4 files of 150 MB plus 1,000 files of 200 KB), upload throttled to 8 MB/s, checkpoint every 10 seconds.
2. As soon as the checkpoint had collected its entries, I made data-pack writes fail, then restored storage after the first pack upload gave up.
3. When the checkpoint's index blob appeared, I killed the process with SIGKILL.
4. A second, unthrottled snapshot of the same folder with nothing injected.
5. A restore of the second snapshot, compared file by file against the source.

## Results

| Run type | Runs | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Pack lost during the checkpoint flush, checkpoint completed with no error, process killed | 9 | The precondition was met each time |
| Of those, second snapshot taken and restored | 8 | Restore exit 0, no errors, 1,004 of 1,004 files identical every time |
| Of those, checkpoint read back in full before any second snapshot | 1 | One entry had missing content: the partial entry for the large file still being uploaded |
| Same sequence with 3,000 small files only | 8 | The checkpoint reported the failure every time; the silent case never arose |

- **The second snapshot did reuse the checkpoint.** It took between 378 and 722 files from the checkpoint without reading them, in seven of the eight restored runs. In the other one no checkpoint manifest survived the kill, so everything was re-read.
- **The low-level defect is real.** `Flush()` does return success after losing a pack, and the checkpoint manifest is committed without reporting it.
- **The data-loss consequence did not happen.** The one dangling reference found belonged to a file that was mid-upload. Kopia stores such files in a checkpoint under a randomised name precisely so later snapshots never reuse them, so the second snapshot re-read that file in full.
- **Why completed files were not affected in these runs.** Before a checkpoint flushes, it waits for every in-progress file's pending writes and fails loudly if one errors. The only packs still in flight at flush time were started after that wait.
- **What remains unproven.** I could not make a completed file's data land in the lost pack, and I cannot prove it is impossible. It would need a pack to roll over in the few milliseconds between the checkpoint collecting its entries and the flush starting.

One real but minor effect remains: restoring the incomplete checkpoint snapshot itself would fail for that one partial file.

content.text:
Item 4 is retained: I reproduced the case you described end to end, and the second snapshot reported success but could not be restored.

## Item 4, reproduced

One large file (150 MB) was still uploading while 40,000 small files finished alongside it. Upload was throttled to 8 MB/s with a checkpoint every 6 seconds, and I made data-pack writes fail from the moment the checkpoint had collected its entries until the first pack upload gave up.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Snapshot 1, checkpoint flush | One 21 MB pack failed to upload. The checkpoint still committed and reported no checkpoint error. |
| Process killed (SIGKILL) | Repository holds an incomplete checkpoint listing 33,662 files. |
| Read every file in the checkpoint | 13,252 completed files and 2 partial-file entries point at data that was never stored. |
| Restore the checkpoint | Fails, exit 1, "content not found". |
| Snapshot 2, healthy storage | Exit 0, marked complete, 0 errors. It reused 33,660 files from the checkpoint without reading them. |
| Restore snapshot 2 | Fails, exit 1, "content not found". |
| Restore snapshot 2 with `--ignore-errors` | Exit 0, but 13,252 of 40,001 files are missing; the other 26,749 are identical to the source. |
| Snapshot 3 | Exit 0; the same 13,252 files are still unrecoverable. |

The missing data matches the one lost pack: five pack uploads succeeded and five are on disk; the sixth is absent.

Both of your points hold:
- Restoring from the checkpoint is a failed restore; my earlier runs already showed the checkpoint referencing missing data and I was wrong to treat that as minor.
- A completed file's data can be in the lost pack, and when it is, every later snapshot inherits the hole until those files change.

How reachable it is:
- It needs three things together: a pack upload that fails for good during a checkpoint flush, that upload having started after the checkpoint collected its entries, and the process dying before the next successful flush.
- With the setup above, it took two attempts.
- In four other setups, about 13 further silent checkpoints either lost only the in-progress file's partial entry or restored clean, and about 35 attempts ended with the checkpoint reporting the failure.

## Definitive list

### New bugs (12, all reproduced)

| Item | What | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | Pack deletion can delete a just-committed pack over 24h old | `repo/maintenance/pack_gc.go:79` |
| 4 | `Flush()` reports success after losing a pack during a checkpoint; later snapshots reuse the dangling entries and cannot be restored | `repo/content/content_manager.go:636-658`, `snapshot/upload/upload.go:541-551,851` |
| 5 | Repository write failure drops the file and the snapshot is saved as complete | `snapshot/upload/upload.go:987-999` |
| 7 | S3 `PutBlob` can store a zero-byte object and report success (role or web-identity credentials) | `repo/blob/s3/s3_storage.go:200-208` |
| 10 | Manifest compaction from a stale view resurrects deleted snapshots and policies | `repo/manifest/committed_manifest_manager.go:211-281` |
| 11 | With duplicate policies, expiration uses the oldest while the editor shows the newest | `snapshot/policy/policy_manager.go:69-75,149` |
| — | keep-daily and the other period settings keep fewer than the documented "most-recent N" after a gap | `snapshot/policy/retention_policy.go:69-83` |
| — | A manifest delete loses to an entry written by a faster clock | `repo/manifest/manifest_manager.go:240-244` |
| — | Checkpoint failure exits 0 and skips remaining sources | `upload.go:569-573`, `cli/command_snapshot_create.go:144-147` |
| — | keep-hourly of 2,562,048 or more keeps nothing; negative values are accepted | `retention_policy.go:203`, `cli/command_policy_set.go:208` |
| — | Server: a retention error discards the snapshot just taken | `internal/server/source_manager.go:397-404` |
| — | Server: sources are treated as local by hostname alone | `internal/server/server.go:1026` |

### Already reported upstream (7)

| What | Upstream |
|---|---|
| Weekly and monthly buckets share ID strings (item 9) | Issue #2964, fix PR #5769 |
| keep-latest above about 2025 collides with the annual bucket | Same root cause; PR #5769 |
| Weekly bucket uses local time, others use UTC (item 12) | Fix PR #5455 |
| Sub-folder policy replaces inherited settings | Issue #5763, fix PR #5766 |
| Server: failed scheduled snapshot skips the retry backoff | Issue #5521 |
| Windows junctions and other reparse points not backed up | Issue #5074 |
| S3 listing can return folder prefixes as blob IDs | Issue #5711 |

### By design (10)

| What |
|---|
| A backup suspended about three days loses data it had uploaded (item 1) |
| A pack uploaded just before a sleep of four days or more is deleted (item 3) |
| Maintenance ownership is a `user@host` string with a machine-local lock (item 8) |
| A snapshot with unreadable source files is saved as complete and counts for retention |
| Retention applies only to snapshot roots |
| Daily, monthly and annual buckets are in UTC |
| Same `user@host` and path on two laptops is one retention group |
| One unreadable manifest blob fails listing on every client |
| `--safety=none` is unsafe with active clients |
| Windows: sockets, devices and unknown entry types are skipped by default |

### Dropped

- **Snapshot GC ignoring an unloadable manifest:** only reproducible with a hand-written manifest.
- **Index compaction ignoring iteration errors:** not reproducible; damaged index blobs are rejected first.
- **Object lock with a fast laptop clock:** not tested, because no S3 server with object lock could be run here.

All test data and the built binary have been removed, and the repository tree is clean.
